headlines.title: 10월 국고채 금리 , 전 구간 하락 …외인 8.5조 순매수

key_headlines.title: TSMC October Revenue Hits Record High on AI Boom
key_headlines.summary: Taiwan's TSMC achieved record October sales with 60% growth driven by artificial intelligence demand, benefiting from global AI chip surge.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's large corporations experienced explosive export growth in Q3 2026, driven primarily by semiconductor sector strength, with exports more than doubling compared to the previous year. However, this manufacturing boom has failed to benefit youth employment, as workers aged 29 and below continue experiencing declining job registrations for the 50th consecutive month. The government's modular housing initiative, promoted as a rapid housing supply solution, encountered its first setback when the housing authority failed to secure a constructor due to uncompetitive project economics. Additionally, major Korean battery manufacturers Samsung SDI and LG Energy Solution expanded their global supply chains significantly with new BMW contracts for European and North American production.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The Bank of Korea maintained its base rate at 3% while over half of its monetary policy committee members signaled the need for further rate tightening to address inflationary pressures and financial stability concerns. Analysis suggests that semiconductor sector bonuses worth 70 trillion won will have limited GDP contribution of around 0.1% due to increased import spending. In the United States, October consumer prices rose 0.4% month-over-month, exceeding market expectations and raising the likelihood of a December Federal Reserve rate increase. The Fed continues monitoring inflation and employment data closely before determining its policy path for the remainder of the year.
sections.Financial Markets: South Korea's stock markets rebounded strongly on November 10, with KOSPI rising 4.39% to 5,239.13 and KOSDAQ gaining 4.48% to 667.61, marking the first positive close in four trading days. The rebound was led by semiconductor stocks, with Samsung Electronics rising 4.74% and SK Hynix gaining 6.69%, supported by positive sentiment from US market recovery. Program buy-side circuit breakers were triggered early in the session due to rapid 5% rallies. Volatility is expected to continue through year-end as market sentiment remains sensitive to price movements and external economic indicators.
sections.Industry & Technology: Korean battery manufacturers secured major global supply contracts, with Samsung SDI and LG Energy Solution entering agreements with BMW to supply high-voltage battery cells from European and US production facilities starting in the late 2020s. LS MnM completed a new refinery facility in Onsan focusing on electric vehicle battery materials including nickel sulfate and cobalt sulfate. Posco is expanding into energy and new materials sectors as traditional steel and secondary battery businesses face headwinds from Chinese oversupply and electric vehicle demand slowdowns. BMW's 'local production, local supply' strategy aims to diversify sourcing and reduce transportation costs while improving supply chain stability.
sections.Real Estate: The government is establishing separate task forces to address deteriorating public sentiment regarding housing policies, particularly concerning charter deposit issues in the Seoul metropolitan area. Real estate application fraud investigations revealed 354 suspicious cases out of 25,000 household applications, including high-income professionals falsely claiming low-income status and fraudulent address changes to secure apartment lottery eligibility. The government maintains that residential property tax benefits must prioritize actual residents over non-resident property owners. Apartment management quality is emerging as a significant factor affecting property values, with well-maintained older complexes appreciating despite their age.
sections.International Economy: The Trump administration is pursuing expanded trade with Myanmar and strategic rare earth supply chain development, targeting tripled US agricultural imports by 2030 and supporting minimum three major commercial investment contracts. Democratic Party think tanks recommend rolling back most Trump-era tariffs on Korean imports, as the party generally favors free trade policies. The Federal Reserve faces mounting inflation concerns despite market expectations of potential rate cuts, with Fed officials emphasizing the need to assess additional price and employment data before determining December policy decisions. International oil prices have declined sharply from $100 to $85 per barrel, reducing inflation pressures and supporting market sentiment.
sections.AI & Economy: Korean telecommunications company KT announced plans to increase AI data center capacity by 1GW by 2031, building on current 152MW operations, with existing pipeline projects totaling 911MW across 20 main locations and 500MW backup capacity. KT's AI transformation initiatives are entering revenue monetization phase in 2027 despite Q3 operating profit declining 6% due to wireless communication sector weakness. Harvard Business School professor Stephen Tomkins warns against reckless AI investment driven by competitive pressure without sufficient experimentation, emphasizing the need for leadership skepticism regarding past success formulas. AI is increasingly recognized as critical infrastructure, with US hyperscaler capital expenditures projected to increase 60% in 2027 to approximately $1.5 trillion, positioning AI infrastructure providers as major beneficiaries.
sections.Others: Taiwan's TSMC achieved record October revenue with 60% growth, reaching all-time high sales driven by global AI chip demand boom. Korean-American Congressman Young Kim lost his House re-election bid in California's 40th district despite intense campaign focus on Trump loyalty and MAGA alignment. HD Hyundai Enersol showed rebound momentum as a weekly investment winner, with market observers expecting Democratic congressional control to slow the Trump administration's plans to phase out clean energy tax credits under the Inflation Reduction Act. The government reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining preferential tax treatment for primary residence properties, clarifying that non-resident property owners will not receive identical basic deductions as actual residents.
